### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A02 appears in about 65% of traces instead of about 21%, and its mean occurrences per trace rise from about 0.22 to 0.70. [OCC001]
- Activity A06 appears in about 7% of traces instead of about 21%, with mean occurrences per trace falling from about 0.23 to 0.07. [OCC002]
- A02 occurs later in traces: its mean relative position moves from about 0.57 to 0.92. [POS001]
- A02 is now almost always followed by A46: the share of A02 outgoing transitions to A46 rises from about 30% to 92%. [DIR001]
- A45 now often leads to A02 instead of A46: A45→A02 rises from about 6% to 63%, while A45→A46 falls from about 84% to 36%. [DIR011]
- A21 and A22 largely stop going to A30: A21→A30 falls from about 51% to 2%, and A22→A30 from about 45% to 1%; they instead go mainly to A24 and A23. [DIR005, DIR006]
- A23 and A24 now almost always go to A30: A23→A30 rises from about 48% to 94%, and A24→A30 from about 51% to 97%. [DIR007, DIR008]
- A29 now goes mainly to A22 and A21 instead of A23 and A24: A29→A22 rises from about 24% to 55%, A29→A21 from about 23% to 43%, while A29→A23 falls from about 27% to 1% and A29→A24 from about 21% to 1%. [DIR009]
- A02 co-occurs with A14, A15, A29, A30, A45 and A46 in about 65% of traces, up from about 21%; in most of those traces the other activity precedes A02, except A46, which follows A02. [REL001, REL002, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Lag patterns confirm the new ordering: A02 immediately precedes A46 in about 99% of relevant pairs versus about 74% before, and A45 immediately precedes A02 in about 100% of relevant pairs versus about 93% before. [LAG002, LAG012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which A02 becomes a common late step that is preceded by several activities and followed by A46, while A06 becomes rare. The routing among A21, A22, A23, A24, A29 and A30 is rearranged so that A21, A22 and A29 feed into A23/A24/A30, which then lead toward A02 and A46. This is supported directly by occurrence, position, successor, co-occurrence and lag indicators that consistently point to the same new ordering. A competing explanation based only on random variant-frequency differences is unlikely given the number and consistency of the distinct differences, although the small number of A06 observations in the later window means the details of A06's new routing are less certain. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR011, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, LAG002, LAG012]
